manuscript_title: Response geometry under community reorganization: from ecological possibility to mechanistic resolution in island plant–pollinator systems
significance_statement: Ecological perturbations are often summarized by average effects even when organisms exposed to the same broad change respond in opposite directions. We show that community reorganization defines a conditional response geometry in which turnover sets the response regime, starting state locates organisms within that geometry, realized community strongly determines cell-level outcomes, local filtering can reallocate response branches, and downstream assurance mainly modifies magnitude. A source-audited confrontation with island systems then identifies the joint measurements required to distinguish these mechanisms, while an Izu deep dive separates composition-level matching structure from unsupported beyond-composition sorting. The framework therefore turns heterogeneous responses from an exception to be averaged away into an ecological object that can be mechanistically decomposed and tested.
